title: Durations
description:
`<chrono>` gives time its own types, so seconds and milliseconds cannot be mixed up by accident.

Write `std::string clockText(std::chrono::seconds total)` that turns a duration into `h:mm:ss`:

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| 3725 s | `"1:02:05"` |
| 59 s | `"0:00:59"` |
| 2 h | `"2:00:00"` |

`std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::hours>(total)` gives the whole hours; subtract them and repeat for minutes. `.count()` turns a duration into a plain number for printing.

Because the parameter is `std::chrono::seconds`, a caller can pass `2h` or `90min` and the conversion is done for them.
